source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Lumbar spinal stenosis with neurogenic claudication that improves when the lumbar spine is flexed","B":"Acute arterial occlusion because symptoms predictably resolve when the client flexes the lumbar spine","C":"Isolated hip osteoarthritis because forward spinal flexion specifically relieves intra-articular hip disease","D":"Peripheral neuropathy because positional relief with sitting is the defining pattern of distal neuropathy"}}
source_row.rationale: Neurogenic claudication from lumbar spinal stenosis commonly worsens with standing or lumbar extension and improves with sitting or forward flexion. The positional pattern helps distinguish it from other causes of leg discomfort.
source_row.source_detail: History and Physical: symptoms worsened by extension/standing or walking and relieved by flexion/sitting; accessed 2026-08-14.

source_row.stem: A client has leg pain and numbness that worsen with standing or walking and improve with sitting or leaning forward. Which disorder best fits this pattern?
